data.title: Media and Equipment Disposal Uncontrolled
data.summary: Decommissioned equipment and storage media left the organisation without verified erasure or destruction, and awaiting-disposal equipment was stored in areas with little access control.
data.description:
Disposal is where data leaves the organisation legitimately and unaccountably. Devices are retired in batches, stacked somewhere convenient, and collected by a contractor whose certificate of destruction nobody reconciles against a list of serial numbers.

The data on them is rarely gone. Deleting files and reinstalling an operating system leaves recoverable content; drives pulled from failed machines are often not erased at all because the machine would not boot; and the long tail — backup tapes, old phones, printer and copier drives, network appliances with configuration and credentials in flash — is usually forgotten entirely.

Equipment awaiting collection is the other half: it holds live data and sits in a corridor or a loading bay for weeks.
data.recommendation:
* Erase to a recognised standard, or destroy, and record it against the asset's serial number.
* Reconcile the disposal contractor's certificates against your own list; a certificate you do not check is paperwork.
* Store awaiting-disposal equipment in a controlled area, treated as live.
* Include printers, copiers, phones and network appliances in the policy — they hold data too.
data.short_recommendation: Destroy or verifiably erase media, and keep certificates.
